subject: Renewal sizing: usage-trigger policy & tranche allocation (Helix Labs)
messages:
From: Amir Khan <amir@helixlabs.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@helixlabs.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:04:12 -0800
Subject: Renewal sizing — unexpected 3x Q3 spike, need guidance

Rishi,

Hope you’re well. Quick note from Helix Ops — our inference traffic spiked in late Sep and held through Oct (3x baseline). We’re approaching our committed capacity floor and seeing queued requests during peak windows. We have the renewal coming up in January and needed to understand: is there a recommended path to convert some of our burst usage into a committed tranche?

High-level asks:
- Can you help map our current utilization to recommended tranche sizes?
- Do you have a short bridge option while we finalize the renewal?

I can share logs/summary if helpful. Would appreciate a short call this week.

Thanks,
Amir
VP Engineering, Helix Labs

----
Helix Labs (ops@helixlabs.ai)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Amir Khan <amir@helixlabs.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 10:22:37 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal sizing — unexpected 3x Q3 spike, need guidance

Amir — thanks for the heads up and sorry to hear you’re hitting queued work. We can definitely help with a sizing recommendation and a short-term bridge.

Next steps I propose:
1) Send over a 7–14 day export of token-level and peak qps (if possible). I’ll have Kimberly run it through our usage-to-commit model.
2) Jordan will draft a tranche allocation & pricing sketch based on the usage curve and preferred runway length (3/6/12 months).
3) I’ll schedule a 30-min sync later this week to align.

We can also offer a temporary burst credit (small amount) to avoid customer impact while we finalize numbers — I’ll loop in ops/finance.

Available windows: Thu 11/3 9–11am PT or Fri 11/4 1–3pm PT — which works for you?

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(415) 555-0192

----
On Mon, Nov 30, 2026 at 9:04 AM Amir Khan <amir@helixlabs.ai> wrote:
> Rishi,
>
> Hope you’re well. Quick note from Helix Ops — our inference traffic spiked...
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Dec 2026 14:18:05 -0800
Subject: Internal: helix tranche sketch & utilization attach

Team — per Amir’s note (below) I grabbed a 14-day summary they provided and pushed it to our Drive. Kimberly, can you run the usage curve->commit sizing model and include a sensitivity table? Jordan, please model three runway scenarios (3m/6m/12m) and the price delta vs burst.

Key constraints from Helix:
- They want predictable latency for business-critical flows (can't tolerate queueing > 200ms p50)
- Willing to commit to a partial tranche now if we provide a short bridge for the remainder
- Procurement timeline: legal review by mid-Dec, sign in Jan

Attachment: helix_utilization_Q3_2026.csv (from Helix) — includes peak QPS, average sequence length, token distribution.

Please post your outputs by Tue EOD so I can consolidate for the proposal.

Thanks,
Rishi

----
On Tue, Dec 1, 2026 at 10:22 AM Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com> wrote:
> Amir — thanks for the heads up and sorry to hear...
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Dec 2026 11:03:50 -0800
Subject: Re: Internal: helix tranche sketch & utilization attach

Rishi/Jordan — ran the file through the sizing model. Summary notes:

- Observed burst shape: sharp 3x peak for ~10 days, then 1.6x sustained uplift.
- Effective utilization (tokens/GPU-hour) suggests a 22% higher steady-state consumption vs baseline.
- Suggested immediate tranche to cover steady uplift: +8 GPUs (A100-equivalent) for 12 months.
- For latency-critical flows, recommend reserving 2 hot-standby GPUs (pre-warmed) and enabling prefix KV caching for the most common prompts — reduces tail latency and lowers token churn.

Sensitivity table (attached in Drive): 3m runway -> recommend temporary +12 GPUs then reduce to +6; 6m runway -> +10 then to +8; 12m runway -> +8 steady. Pricing delta included in the sheet.

I’ll convert into a short PDF we can send to Helix.

-Kim
Staff Product Manager, Redwood Console
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Amir Khan <amir@helixlabs.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Dec 2026 09:47:23 -0800
Subject: Proposal: tranche allocation + short bridge (Helix Labs renewal)

Amir — thanks for the data. Attached is our proposal (redwood_tranche_proposal_v2.pdf) summarizing:

- Recommended commitment: +8 A100-equivalent GPUs (12-month tranche) to address the sustained uplift and normalize unit economics.
- Short-term bridge: a 30-day temporary burst buffer of 12 GPUs (no change to billing cadence; priced as burst credit) to cover immediate peak windows while procurement finishes.
- Latency controls: reserve 2 hot-standby GPUs and enable prefix KV caching for the two latency-sensitive routes you flagged.
- Pricing note: effective per-GPU discount for the 12-month tranche vs on-demand burst; details in the attached.

We understand procurement is tight; to expedite legal review I’ve included a one-page SOW excerpt with standard terms (sow_terms_excerpt.txt) and a DocuSign link below. If this looks good, we can lock the tranche and start onboarding the reserve GPUs within 72 hours.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/HLX-2026-Tranche-V2
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/hlx-util-reports

Best,
Rishi
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

----
Attachment: redwood_tranche_proposal_v2.pdf
From: Amir Khan <amir@helixlabs.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@helixlabs.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2026 09:20:04 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: tranche allocation + short bridge (Helix Labs renewal)

Rishi — appreciate the quick turnaround. Proposal looks reasonable; two asks before we sign:

1) Can you add an explicit SLA note for the latency-critical routes (p50/p95 targets and credits)?
2) Would Redwood consider a 1-month discounted burst-credit (reduce the bridge cost by 20%) given this is effectively an emergency top-up?

If we can get those two items we can move legal review forward today.

Thanks,
Amir
VP Engineering, Helix Labs
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2026 16:12:09 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: tranche allocation + short bridge (Helix Labs renewal) — internal approval

Rishi — reviewed the ask. Approve: 1-month 20% concession on the burst buffer and a short SLA addendum for the latency routes (standard credit schedule) provided legal signs off on the SOW excerpt. Keep the reserve onboarding as a provisional change until we get signed docs.

Note: finance wants to track this as a one-off concession against the Q4 quota; please tag HLX-2026-RW-3 in the reconciliation sheet.

V.
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
